README: A whole-piece reading: every mark an edition prints for one fugue, in every voice and bar, attached to the game's own notes.

Notes are addressed as in data/touch/pieces.json: v = voice index (here 0 Soprano, 1 Alto, 2 Bass, pieces.json voiceNames), on = onset tick (tpq 1920; a 4/4 bar is 7680 ticks; bar starts as in pieces.json bars[]). p (MIDI) and name are a check (names are the game's spelling, even where the edition renotates), bar and pos (sixteenths from the barline) are for people.

marks[]: one note's articulation. art is one of staccato (dot), wedge (Keil: shorter and sharper), tenuto (dash: full value, a slight lean), portato (dash over dot: held a little apart, each note weighted), accent (>), marcato (^ over a dot: struck hard and left), fermata. A note may have two marks (wedge+tenuto).

slurs[]: spans in one voice, from and to both included. kind "slur" = a group played as one gesture (joined inside, the last note lighter and, with lastShort, let go early); kind "portato" = dots under a slur (each note detached a little but carried in one line); kind "phrase" = a long phrasing arc over a whole subject or line. role says what the slur covers.
dyn[]: a printed level at a time, for the voices it was printed for (Busoni prints dynamics per staff, sometimes per voice).

hairpins[]: cresc/dim spans in time for the given voices. text[]: words printed in the score with an English gloss. tempo.changes[] is left empty on purpose: the owner has ruled out tempo warping except at fermatas, so Busoni's tempo words are kept only in tempo.notes[] (applied: false) and fermatas stay in marks[].

breaths[]: a printed caesura before a note. voicing[]: pianistic re-voicings, recorded as notes only and not to be applied: octave-doubling (interval in semitones) and added notes. ornaments[]: a printed ornament and how Busoni realises it.
rules[]: instructions that apply to unmarked notes; the game must apply these by rule. sections[]: Busoni's double bars.
fingering: a summary of patterns and a few samples (fingers in the order of the notes from that note on); not every digit is transcribed.
footnotes[]: German text (as printed, old spelling kept) and an English translation.
conf on every item: sure (clearly printed and placed), likely (printed, the placement or the sign read from a 300 dpi scan with some doubt), unsure (a guess: hard to see, or inferred).
This format is a superset of docs/wtc/readings/*.json: the old per-note subject marks can be derived from marks[] and slurs[] on the first entry.
title: Fugue 18 in G♯ minor, BWV 887

edition.author: Ferruccio B. Busoni
edition.title: Des wohltemperierten Klavieres zweiter Teil (J. S. Bach, Klavierwerke, Busoni-Ausgabe, Band II)

character: Double fugue, "a due soggetti": Fuga I (b.1), Fuga II (b.61.4, a tempo), Fuga I e II (b.97). "mezza voce egualmente e tutto legato"; the close "espressivo ma semplicemente".
dynamicPlan: Mezza voce throughout; small swells (b.20, 22); cresc. (b.25) and dim. (b.27); cresc. to the bass trill (b.30–31); swells on the alto (b.45–48); dim. hairpins (b.107–110); espressivo ma semplicemente (b.139), sostenendo to the end with hairpins (b.140–141).

text.text: mezza voce egualmente e tutto legato
text.en: half voice, even, and all legato
sustained (footnote 1: the following six bars are an inserted parenthesis)

rules.art: legato throughout ("tutto legato"); each subject entry under one phrasing arc
brought out a little (voicing, not articulation)

ornaments.name: B2
ornaments.realisation: no realisation printed; a long trill on the bass B

ornaments.name: E2
ornaments.realisation: no realisation printed; trill on the held bass E closing Fuga I

ornaments.name: C##5
ornaments.realisation: trill closed by the written grace notes (B♯–C𝄪)

ornaments.name: F##4
ornaments.realisation: no realisation printed; bracketed, an editorial suggestion

ornaments.name: B#3
ornaments.realisation: no realisation printed; bracketed, an editorial suggestion

ornamentsNote: Trills at b.30 and b.60 (bass) and b.64 (soprano, closed by grace notes); bracketed (tr) at b.69 and b.74. Skipped: "Idee:" staves (b.37–41, 69–73, 92–96), the NB variant (b.83) and the analytic footnotes and commentary on p.59.

summary: Not transcribed (economy brief: gameplay does not use fingering).

footnotes.de: Die Mittelstimme für die nächsten vier Takte etwas hervorgehoben.
footnotes.en: Bring out the middle voice a little for the next four bars.

caveats: Economy reading from 200 dpi system crops of the 1915 Breitkopf print; fingering and "Idee" staves skipped.
Busoni marks this fugue sparsely: legato, phrasing arcs over entries, a few hairpins. Inner-voice slurs and small ties are not transcribed.
"sostenendo" at b.59 (end of Fuga I) and "sostenuto" at b.90 are mid-piece tempo words and are not applied; "a tempo" follows at b.61.
notes: Game import (WTC 1.91, D394): "1) middle voice brought out" (bar 41) dropped from text: footnote 1's gloss (footnotes are not played), not printed words.
